'''Visuals:''' This logo consists of either the Nintendo logo with an oblong shape on either a black or white background or copyright information for the company below the title screen of the game.

'''Variants:'''
* On many arcade, SNES, Nintendo 64, Game Boy, Game Boy Color and NES titles, the logo wordmark appears within a copyright notice.
* On the arcade games of ''Punch-Out!'' and ''Super Punch-Out!'', a larger Nintendo oblong shape appears below the title screen.
* Sometimes, on early arcade titles, the text instead says "Nintendo of America, Inc."
* On ''Mario Kart Wii'', the logo is in the bottom right corner of the screen.
* On some early SNES games, like ''Super Mario Kart'', ''Yoshi's Safari'', ''Super Punch-Out!!'' (this game has the logo in silver), and ''Stunt Race FX'' (this game has the logo in pink), the logo is smaller.
* On NTSC-J/PAL releases of some Nintendo games, the logo is colored in blue instead of red, simillar to [[Nintendo (Commercial Tags)#2nd Tag (1986-1998)|1986-1998 Japanese Nintendo commercial tags]].
* Some NTSC-J/PAL releases of games, like ''Donkey Kong Jr.'', have the logo appearing in silver.
* On the ''New Super Mario Bros.'' title screen, copyright information for Nintendo fades in below after the ''NSMB'' logo forms by falling down one-by-one as Mario tries to save Princess Peach from being kidnapped; a turtle shell appears from the right of the screen behind Mario, thus hitting him and causing him to shrink. He then jumps to hit the logo, straightening the letters' positions and going after Peach and Jr. as the logo's shadows fade in.
* On ''Super Mario 64'', the Super Mario 64 logo pops up before zooming out and fading away, with copyright information for Nintendo seen below.
* On most ''Kirby'' games, it is paired with the [[HAL Laboratory]] logo or the Halken logo. It is also paired with HAL in some Smash Bros. games.
* On ''Kirby and the Forgotten Land'', it is superimposed on the end of the opening cutscene with the HAL logo.
* On the American version of Nintendo DS games of ''Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games'' and ''Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Winter Games'', "in cooperation with" is shown above the logo.
* At the end of the ''Pikmin Short Movies'' "Occupational Hazards" and "Treasure in a Bottle", the logo is still and white on a black background. 
** On many games such as ''Mariokart: Double Dash!!'' and its successor ''Mariokart DS'', the logo fades in and out.
* A version redone in CGI exists, where the logo is placed over a black background. This variant is primarily seen on [[Nintendo 64]] material such as ''Donkey Kong 64''.

'''Technique:''' A sprite-based graphic. The CGI variant uses real-time 3D computer graphics.

'''Audio:''' None or the opening theme of the game.

'''Audio Variants:'''
* An enhanced version of the coin collect sound effect from the Mario series is heard on ''Super Mario 64'', ''Super Mario Sunshine'', ''New Super Mario Bros.'', and ''Super Mario 64 DS'', respectively.
* On ''Super Mario 64'', Mario is also heard saying "It's-a-me, Mario!".
* On ''Mario Kart DS'', two sped up engine sounds are heard, followed by Mario shouting "Yahoo!".
* On ''Stunt Race FX'', a honking sound effect is heard.
* On ''Super Punch-Out!!'', a bling sound akin to the Game Boy startup the is heard.
* On ''New Super Mario Bros.'' (DS), after the coin sound from the variant mentioned above plays, the title screen music is heard over rattling sounds and a bicycle horn sound from the General Series 6000 library, as well as a series of squeaks for Bowser Jr. when he walks/runs and enhanced SFX from the original ''New Super Mario Bros.'' game.
* On ''Donkey Kong 64'', Donkey Kong says "Ok!".
* On ''Luigi's Mansion'', a deep voice says the company name.
* On ''Mario Kart: Double Dash!!'', Mario shouts "NIIIIIINTENDOOOOOO!!!! Woohoo!", which continues on to the [[Dolby Surround]] logo.

'''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' 
* The logo's wordmark first appeared on the arcade game of ''Donkey Kong Jr.'', and went on to appear on various console games, beginning with the NES game of ''Punch-Out!'', and appeared on several games, like the Nintendo NES game of ''Tetris'', the NES games of ''Super Mario Bros. 3'' and ''Dr. Mario'', the Game Boy games of ''Super Mario Land'' and ''Baseball'', and the SNES game of ''Pilotwings'', among others.
* The logo with the oblong shape first appeared properly on the European version of ''Solstice'' (NES), as well as the U.S. version of ''NCAA Basketball'' (SNES).
* The small version can be found on ''Super Mario Kart'', ''Super Mario All-Stars (+ Super Mario World)'', ''Stunt Race FX'', ''Super Punch-Out!!'', ''Yoshi's Safari'', and ''Super Mario All-Stars 25th Anniversary Edition''.
* It can also be found on most Nintendo games and their title screens such as ''Paper Mario'', ''Mario Party 5'', ''The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker'', among others.
* A non-game appearance of this logo can be spotted at the end of the ''Pikmin Short Movies'' "Occupational Hazards" and "Treasure in a Bottle".
** The shorts were previously sold on the 3DS app ''Pikmin Short Movies 3D'' and Wii U app ''Pikmin Short Movies HD'', but both have since been delisted from the eShop, and they can now be viewed on Nintendo's YouTube channel.
** The third short, "The Night Juicer", also does not have the logo or any credits, likely due to its shorter length.
* In most relatively recent games such as ''New Super Mario Bros. Wii'', the logo is absent, but it still shows up occasionally, such as on ''Kirby and the Forgotten Land''.
** Also in ''Super Mario 3D World'', the copyright text for this logo can be found here!

===2nd Logo ({{date|month=November|day=21|year=1990}}-{{date|month=October|day=21|year=2003}})===
[[File:Vlcsnap-2015-04-26-12h25m52s220.png|300px|center]]

'''Visuals:''' Over a black background is "- Nintendo -" in its corporate font without the oblong shape. Below it is "Presents".

'''Technique:''' A sprite-based graphic.

'''Audio:''' A random sound effect from the game.
* On ''Super Mario World'' and ''Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island'' for SNES, the coin collect sound effect from the game is heard.
* On ''Yoshi's Island: Super Mario Advance 3'', Yoshi says the word "Nintendo", which is taken from ''Yoshi's Story''.
* On ''Yoshi's Story'', a chorus of Yoshis say "Nintendo".
* On ''The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past'', the Rupee collect sound effect from the game plays.
* On ''Super Scope 6'', none.

'''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' 
* This logo can be found on ''Super Mario World'', ''Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island'', ''Yoshi's Story'', ''The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past'', ''Super Scope 6'', ''Super Mario Advance 2: Super Mario World'', ''Super Mario Advance 3: Yoshi's Island'', ''Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3'' and ''Pokémon FireRed''.
* However, on ''Super Mario Advance'', there is no Nintendo logo at all.

===4th Logo ({{date|month=July|day=14|year=1993}}-December 1994; {{date|month=December|day=12|year=2010}})===
[[File:Nintendo (1992).png|center|300px]]

'''Visuals:''' Over a black background is the normal Nintendo logo, but the oblong shape is stretched out a bit. On top of the text is a gold Mario coin that shines once.

'''Technique:''' Sprite-based 2D animation.

'''Audio:''' The coin sound effect from the 2nd logo. 

'''Availability:''' This logo can be found on ''Super Mario All-Stars (+ Super Mario World)'' for the SNES and ''Super Mario All-Stars 25th Anniversary Edition'' for the Wii.

===5th Logo ({{date|month=December|day=14|year=1996}}-{{date|month=February|day=10|year=1997}})===
<tabber>

'''Visuals:''' Over a black background the Nintendo logo in gold is seen spinning around, going faster and faster until it creates motion blur. Finally, while the Nintendo logo is still spinning, it fades out to reveal an empty, white background.

'''Technique:''' Real-time 3D CGI combined with computer animated CGI effects.

'''Audio:''' Some racing car sounds.

'''Availability:''' This logo was exclusively made for ''Mario Kart 64'' and it can be found on both the Japanese and American version of the game.

===6th Logo (''Perfect Dark'' custom variant) ({{date|month=May|day=22|month2=June|day2=30|year=2000}})===
[[File:ZNJgt9YxYN0KtBXReyXRJA21962.png|center|350px]]
{{YouTube|id=UzqsdLPBFwU}}

'''Visuals:''' The sequence starts on a black background. A light brightens up, revealing a silver version of the Nintendo logo, slowly rotating on its y-axis, as the light slowly dims and becomes dark again.

'''Technique:''' In-engine animation.

'''Audio:''' A whoosh sound.

'''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' This logo is only seen on ''Perfect Dark''.

===7th Logo (''Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem'' custom variant) ({{date|month=June|day=23|month2=November|day2=7|year=2002}})===
<gallery mode="packed" heights="200">
Nintendo (2002, America).png
Nintendo (2002, PAL).png
</gallery>
{{YouTube|id=IQRlJ_rZHvM|id2=wjg3vazLdGg}}
{{guidance detail|reason=jumpscare(0:04),audio}}

'''Visuals:''' Over a black background is some reddish-gray smoke rising, forming a red skeleton with its eyes lit green, which then looks to the camera with its mouth opening. Its eyes brighten up before a cyan flash of light appears, causing the skeleton to melt to the right, off the screen. The flash becomes a beam of light, circling around before it reaches the bottom-center of an outline of the Nintendo logo. It flashes even brighter and the full Nintendo logo appears in light blue. Throughout its screen time, the color of the Nintendo logo changes to red.

'''Variant:''' On the Japanese and PAL/European versions of the game, the Nintendo logo would turn blue instead of red.

'''Technique:''' CGI.

'''Audio:''' Ominous orchestral music, accompanied by the skeleton growling. After a phasing sound when the Nintendo logo gets formed, a deep "thud" is heard and a deep male announcer says the company name.

'''Availability:{{Hidden cat}}''' This logo is only seen on ''Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem'' for the Nintendo GameCube.
